constraints: tree-sitter-php crate version must pass cargo deny check without SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK (package >=7 days old)
PHP grammar uses base_clause and class_interface_clause as child nodes, not fields on class_declaration
No parent_class, base_classes, or interfaces fields exist in tree-sitter-php grammar; must walk children or use named_child iteration
HTML-embedded PHP (<?php ... ?> mixed with HTML) must parse with zero ERROR nodes and yield same elements as PHP-only equivalent
DEFUSE_QUERY is required per acceptance criteria and issue scope; must cover local declarations, assignments, and identifier reads
Only .php extension in scope; .phtml, .inc, .module, .php5 explicitly out of scope
No trait use resolution, property/constant extraction, attributes, or namespace aliasing in scope

library_findings.version: Latest available (to be determined from crates.io; must be >=7 days old)
library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE constant; node kinds: class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration, function_definition, method_declaration; fields: name, body; child nodes: base_clause, class_interface_clause, declaration_list
library_findings.notes: Grammar uses base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) as direct children of class_declaration, not as fields. base_clause and class_interface_clause contain comma-separated name nodes. function_definition is the top-level function node kind. method_declaration is for class methods. use_declaration captures namespace imports.

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter::Language, tree_sitter::Node, tree_sitter::Query, tree_sitter::QueryCursor, node.child_by_field_name(), node.named_child(), node.child_count(), node.start_byte(), node.end_byte()
library_findings.notes: Query syntax uses @capture names and field: syntax to match specific node fields. Queries compile at runtime with Query::new(). Node bounds must be checked before byte-range extraction from source.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Direct base_clause/class_interface_clause child walk
approaches.description: Extract inheritance by iterating all children of class_declaration, checking for base_clause and class_interface_clause node kinds, then iterating their named_child() to collect name nodes. Simpler than field-based extraction since PHP grammar does not expose these as fields.
pros: Aligns with actual tree-sitter-php grammar structure
No field-name lookups that would fail
Handles multiple implements clauses naturally via iteration
Proven pattern in Swift handler (inheritance_specifier children)
cons: Requires manual child iteration rather than field_by_name lookup
More verbose than Java's field-based approach

approaches.name: Approach 2: Query-based inheritance extraction
approaches.description: Use tree-sitter queries to capture base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes directly, avoiding manual child iteration. Queries would match (base_clause (name) @extends) and (class_interface_clause (name) @implements), then extract captured nodes in extract_inheritance.
pros: Easier to test query syntax independently
cons: Adds complexity to extract_inheritance (must run queries inside handler)
Queries must be compiled per call (performance cost)
Less common pattern in existing handlers (Java uses fields, Swift uses children)

approaches.name: Approach 3: Minimal handler with no inheritance extraction
approaches.description: Implement php.rs with only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY; set extract_inheritance to None in LanguageInfo. Meets acceptance criteria for element extraction and imports but skips inheritance analysis.
pros: Fastest to implement (no inheritance walk logic)
Acceptable if inheritance analysis is not a priority
cons: Fails acceptance criterion: extract_inheritance must return ['extends Bar', 'implements A', 'implements B'] for class Foo extends Bar implements A, B
Inconsistent with Java/Swift handlers which both implement inheritance
Limits usefulness for codebase analysis tasks

recommendation: Approach 1 (Direct base_clause/class_interface_clause child walk). The tree-sitter-php grammar exposes inheritance via child nodes (base_clause, class_interface_clause) rather than fields, making field-based extraction impossible. Approach 1 aligns with the actual grammar structure, follows the Swift precedent for child-based inheritance extraction, and is simpler than query-based extraction. The handler will iterate class_declaration children, check for base_clause and class_interface_clause node kinds, then collect name nodes from each, prefixing them with 'extends' or 'implements' respectively. This approach satisfies all acceptance criteria including the inheritance extraction test case.

inheritance_walk_citation: Walk the class_declaration node's children via node.child(i) iteration. For each child, check if child.kind() == "base_clause"; if so, iterate its named_child(j) to collect name nodes and prefix each with "extends ". Then check if child.kind() == "class_interface_clause"; if so, iterate its named_child(j) to collect name nodes and prefix each with "implements ". This pattern is documented in tree-sitter-php's grammar rule: class_declaration contains optional($.base_clause) and optional($.class_interface_clause) as direct children (not fields), and base_clause/class_interface_clause each contain commaSep1($._name), meaning one or more name nodes separated by commas.
